description: We are a closed team of two working on an early-warning system that integrates NASA’s satellite and water resource data to monitor water quality, pollution, and drought risks. Our project focuses on mapping and tracking environmental data to help authorities respond faster. We are not looking for new members at the moment.
summary:
AquaNet Monitor is an intelligent early-warning platform designed to tackle climate-driven water scarcity and environmental degradation. The project leverages official NASA satellite data—specifically NASA GRACE for tracking groundwater shifts and long-term droughts, and NASA MODIS for monitoring surface water anomalies and pollution signs.

By automatically translating these complex data streams into intuitive, color-coded map alerts (such as flagging high-risk drought or pollution zones in red), AquaNet Monitor provides local authorities and decision-makers with real-time visibility. This enables them to spot critical water crises early, take proactive steps, and protect vital water resources before situations escalate.
details:
What does it do & How does it work? AquaNet Monitor is an intelligent early-warning mapping platform designed to monitor water quality, drought patterns, and environmental shifts. The system works by ingesting open-source NASA satellite data—specifically NASA GRACE (for tracking regional groundwater storage changes) and NASA MODIS / Worldview (for observing surface water anomalies and pollution signs). It automatically translates these complex satellite readings into clear, intuitive color-coded alerts on an interactive map (such as flagging high-risk drought or pollution zones in red).

Benefits & Intended Impact: The platform shifts water management from reactive crisis response to proactive protection. By providing real-time, easy-to-read visual indicators, it empowers local authorities, environmental agencies, and communities to spot critical water stress early and take immediate preventive action before crises escalate.

Tools & Creativity: Our team utilized open NASA Earth observation datasets alongside modern web mapping and visualization concepts (prototyped using Canva and Google Workspace) to make complex scientific satellite data accessible and actionable at a single glance for non-technical decision-makers.
